name: app.R
content:
# app.R

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(pracma)
library(shinyvalidate)
library(ggsci)
library(PKNCA)

# ---- UI ----
ui <- fluidPage(
  
  # titlePanel("PK Profile Simulator"),
  titlePanel(
    title = div(
      img(src = "https://styleguide.ugent.be/files/uploads/logo_UGent_EN_RGB_2400_kleur_witbg.png", height = "80px"),
      "One Compartment PK model - IV Bolus Administration",
      style = "display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0px;"
    )
  ),
  
  
  fluidRow(
    column(width = 3,
           wellPanel(style = "height: 85vh; overflow-y: auto;",
                     
                     tags$h3("Drug A", style= "color: #1E64C8;"),
                     numericInput("dose1", "Dose (mg)", value = 100),
                     # numericInput("ke1", "Elimination rate constant ke (1/h)", value = 0.2),
                     numericInput("cl1", "Clearance CL (L/h)", value = 2),
                     numericInput("V1", "Volume of Distribtion Vd (L)", value = 10),
                     
                     hr(style = "border-top: 1px solid #000000;"),
                     
                     tags$h3("Drug B", style= "color: #F1A42B;"),
                     numericInput("dose2", "Dose (mg)", value = 100),
                     # numericInput("ke2", "Elimination rate constant ke (1/h)", value = 0.2),
                     numericInput("cl2", "Clearance CL (L/h)", value = 2),
                     numericInput("V2", "Volume of Distribtion Vd (L)", value = 10),
                     
                     hr(style = "border-top: 1px solid #000000;"),
                     
                     h3("Plot"),
                     numericInput("t_max", "Time Range (h):", value = 24, step = 1),
                     checkboxInput("log_scale", "Logarithmic Scale for Y-Axis", value = TRUE),
                     checkboxInput("MEC_plot", "Plot minimal effective concentration (MEC)", value = FALSE),
                     numericInput("MEC", "MEC (mg/L)", value = 5, step = 0.1),
           )),
    
    
    column(width = 6,
           wellPanel(
             
             plotOutput("pkPlot"),
             br(),
             tableOutput("pkTable")
           )
    ),
    
    column(width = 3,
           wellPanel(
             h3("Supplementary Material:"),
             p("The one-compartment model is the simplest pharmacokinetic model 
    used to describe drug disposition in the body. The core underlying assumption to this model
    is that the body is treated as a single, homogeneous space in which the drug distributes instantaneously
    and uniformly following administration."),
             
             p(
               strong("Instant Distribution:"), " While this represents a significant 
    simplification of reality, it proves surprisingly effective for a wide range of drugs and clinical
    scenarios; particularly those that distribute rapidly from plasma into other body fluids after administration."),
             
             p(
               strong("First-Order Kinetics:"), " The elimination rate is proportional to the 
    remaining concentration. Following IV bolus administration, concentration
          decreases exponentially over time."
             ),
             
             # Skips one line
             tags$br(),
             p(strong("Key Parameters:"), style = "margin-bottom: 5px;"),
             
             # Indents only the key parameters section
             tags$div(
               style = "margin-left: 20px;", 
               p(strong("Vd:"), " Volume of distribution.The volume of distribution does not correspond to any
               real physiological volume but reflects the extent to which a drug distributes into tissues relative
                 to plasma."),
               p(strong("CL:"), " Clearance is the primary pharmacokinetic parameter describing
            the volume of plasma from which drug is completely removed per
            unit time (L/h)."),
               
               p(strong("ke:"), "Elimination rate constant (1/h). It describes the fraction of
            drug eliminated per unit time."),
               
               p(strong("C0:")," Initial plasma concentration immediately after IV bolus
            administration."
               ),
               
               p(strong("t1/2 (Half-life):"), " Time required for the plasma concentration to decrease by 50%.")),
             hr(),
             helpText("Created by the Department of Bioanalysis at Ghent University.")
           ),
    )
  )
)



# ---- SERVER ----
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  # ---- VALIDATION ----
  iv <- InputValidator$new()
  
  
  
  iv$add_rule("dose1", sv_gte(0))
  # iv$add_rule("ke1", sv_gt(0))
  iv$add_rule("cl1", sv_gt(0))
  iv$add_rule("V1", sv_gt(0))
  
  iv$add_rule("dose2", sv_gte(0))
  # iv$add_rule("ke2", sv_gt(0))
  iv$add_rule("cl2", sv_gt(0))
  iv$add_rule("V2", sv_gt(0))
  
  iv$add_rule("t_max", sv_gt(0))
  iv$add_rule("MEC", sv_gt(0))
  iv$enable()
  
  output$pkPlot <- renderPlot({
    req(iv$is_valid())  
    
    # Define time sequence
    time <- seq(0, input$t_max, by = 0.1)
    
    #  ke 
    # ke1 <- input$ke1
    # ke2 <- input$ke2
    ke1 <- input$cl1 / input$V1
    ke2 <- input$cl2 / input$V2
    
    # Initial concentrations
    C01 <- input$dose1 / input$V1
    C02 <- input$dose2 / input$V2
    
    # Concentration-time profiles
    conc1 <- C01 * exp(-ke1 * time)
    conc2 <- C02 * exp(-ke2 * time)
    
    # Create data frame
    df <- data.frame(time = rep(time, 2), 
                     concentration = c(conc1, conc2),
                     set = rep(c("Drug A", "Drug B"), each = length(time)))
    
    # Plot with ggplot
    p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = time, y = concentration, color = set, linetype=set)) +
      geom_line(size = 2) +
      labs(
        x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma concentration (mg/L)",
        colour="",
        linetype="",
        title = expression(C == C[0] *~ e^{-k[e] * t}~"="~~ (frac(D, V)) * e^{-frac(CL,V) * t})) +
      scale_linetype_manual(values=c(1,2))+
      scale_colour_manual(values=c("#1E64C8","#F1A42B"))+
      theme_bw(base_size=20)+
      theme(panel.grid.minor=element_blank(),
            axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
            panel.border = element_blank(),
            legend.position="bottom",legend.key.width=unit(3, 'cm'))
    
    # Apply logarithmic scale if selected
    if (input$log_scale) {
      p <- p + scale_y_log10()
    }
    
    
    # Add MEC if selected 
    if (input$MEC_plot) {
      p <- p    + geom_hline(yintercept = input$MEC, linetype="dotted")+
        annotate("text",x=input$t_max,y=input$MEC,label="MEC", hjust=1, vjust =-1)
    }
    
    print(p)
  })
  
  output$pkTable <- renderTable({
    req(iv$is_valid())  
    
    # Define time sequence
    time <- seq(0, input$t_max, by = 0.1)
    
    # Volumes
    V1 <- input$V1
    V2 <- input$V2
    
    #  ke 
    # ke1 <- input$ke1
    # ke2 <- input$ke2
    ke1 <- input$cl1 / input$V1
    ke2 <- input$cl2 / input$V2
    
    # Calculate concentration-time profile
    conc1 <- (input$dose1 / input$V1) * (exp(-ke1 * time)) 
    conc2 <- (input$dose2 / input$V2) * (exp(-ke2 * time)) 
    
    # Initial concentrations
    C01 <- input$dose1 / input$V1
    C02 <- input$dose2 / input$V2
    
    C0 <- c(C01, C02)
    # Tmax <- c(0, 0)
    
    
    # Exact AUC from time zero to infinity
    # AUC = Dose / CL
    AUC <- c(
      input$dose1 / input$cl1,
      input$dose2 / input$cl2
    )
    
    # Half-life
    t12 <- log(2) / c(ke1, ke2)
    
    # Resulting PK table
    df <- data.frame(
      Drug = c("Drug A", "Drug B"),
      C0 = C0,
      # Tmax = Tmax,
      AUC = AUC,
      ke = c(ke1, ke2),
      t12 = t12
    )
    
    colnames(df) <- c(
      "Drug",
      "C0 (mg/L)",
      # "Tmax (h)",
      "AUC (mg/L.h)",
      "ke (1/h)",
      "t1/2 (h)"
    )
    
    df
  }, digits = 3)
  
}

# Run App
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
